desc: Derive and document the edge-on-path probabilities for a random recursive tree, including the urn-style argument for two endpoints both being in the subtree of `i` when `i < min(u, v)`, and handle endpoint/root special cases.
Implement the complete Python solution with robust input parsing, modular precomputations, prefix arrays, and O(1) query evaluation.

Validate the implementation on the provided samples and brute-force enumeration for small `N`, including edge cases such as `u = 1`, `v = 2`, and adjacent vertices, then fix any coefficient or modulo issues.
If validation reveals a mismatch, re-derive the coefficients via counting/inclusion-exclusion or expected-depth/LCA decomposition and update the formula.
If the closed-form derivation remains uncertain, implement an offline Fenwick/sweep fallback based on edge contributions to cross-check or replace the formula.
